auditor: agent session (Claude), see run record prompts/runs/ for 2026-11-28 quality/0
professional: a CMMC Registered Practitioner who prepares small defense machine shops for a Level 2 self-assessment. They check first that the SPRS score the affirming official will enter is right (point values, partial credits, objectives deciding MET, the SSP rule), then that the POA&M rules for Conditional status are applied exactly as 32 CFR 170.21 words them.

evidence.correctness: Ran a scratch vitest file against src/shared/controls/index.ts (deleted after). Hand arithmetic from DoD Assessment Methodology v1.2.1 and 32 CFR 170.21/170.24 rules: 3.1.1 not implemented + 3.1.3 partial (no credit) + 3.5.3 MFA partial = 110-5-1-3 = 101 (observed 101); 3.13.11 not FIPS = 107 and Conditional-eligible (107, true); 3.1.1 Implemented with objective [a] not met = 105, flagged, and a POA&M blocker (105, flagged, blocker); everything not implemented but the SSP = -203, the published floor (-203); 22 eligible 1-pointers open = 88 eligible, 23 = 87 not (88/true, 87/false); closeout 180 days from 2026-01-15 = 2026-07-14 and from 2028-01-15 (leap) = 2028-07-13 (both match). Weight census 44x5 + 14x3 + 51x1 + 3.12.4 at 0 = 313, consistent with -203. Differential: 2000 random states scored by the app and by the separately written free calculator (apps/cmmc-site/src/sprs.mjs): 0 differences. eCFR, NIST and DoD CIO hosts all refused by the proxy today, so no live re-read of the sources; the prior audit's 110/110 weight match was not repeated.
evidence.completeness: pnpm test:unit 513 passed and pnpm test:worker 166 passed on arrival (vitest 5.1.1); pnpm build (vite) succeeded; pnpm typecheck and biome ci clean. README feature rows checked against the worker suite (controls, score, POA&M eligibility, SSP render, imports, affirmations, ISO 9001, documents, audits, assets, providers, people, suppliers, policies). Billing ships dark until owner secrets (README says so). DEPLOY.md records https://cmmc.marisstella.app/api/health answering; that host was refused by the proxy here, so the served app was not loaded.

evidence.fitness: Walked the job a shop's practitioner does: mark 110 requirements and objectives, get the SPRS score, see which open items may go on a POA&M, generate the SSP and POA&M. All present and right on the cases above. Still missing for a real shop: enduring exceptions and temporary deficiencies under an operational plan of action (32 CFR 170.24(b)(1)), which are assessed as MET; a shop waiting on a FIPS-validated module or with an enduring exception documented in its SSP must mark Implemented with no trace or take the deduction. Not verified live (host refused). Held at 2.
evidence.domain: Compared against DoD Assessment Methodology v1.2.1 (110 start, 5/3/1, the two partial credits, SSP gate) and 32 CFR 170.21(a)(2) and (b), 170.24(b)(2): every rule above applied as worded; a requirement with a not-met objective now scores not met, which is the conservative reading a practitioner expects. Departure: 170.24(b)(1) MET conditions (enduring exception, operational plan of action) not modelled.

Prior defect 5, open on arrival: an objective result, once set, could not be cleared back to unanswered (the select ignored the blank option and the service merge could only add keys). Fixed in this PR: null clears, worker test added.

Prior defect 6, open on arrival: level1.ts is a second hand-typed copy of machine-shop-guides/l1-data.mjs with no test keeping them equal. Comparing them found the texts identical but the objective ids different for single-objective requirements (3.10.4, 3.14.4: bare number on the free page, '[a]' in the app), so a shop moving from the free worksheet to the app sees two ids for one objective. This PR adds level1-parity.test.ts, which pins every text and that this is the only id difference; unifying the ids is left open.
Prior defect 7, open on arrival: flagships.yaml's cmmc entry named private-monorepo as the app's home and listed landed milestones as to build. Fixed in this PR.

New: the objective-conflict list's status guard is untested; dropping it (so not-implemented requirements with a not-met objective are listed as conflicts on the dashboard and in the SSP summary) survived all 513 unit and 166 worker tests. Fixed in this PR with a unit test.

verdict: Meets the bar (correctness 3, claims 3, verification 3, median 3); finished (completeness 3). PR #19893 closed the four defects it marked: a requirement with a not-met objective now scores not met (3.1.1 Implemented with [a] not met gives 105, flagged, and blocks Conditional status), the two POA&M survivors and allMet are now killed by tests, and the citations read 170.21(a)(2)(ii)/(iii). Seven score and POA&M cases match hand arithmetic from the DoD Methodology and 32 CFR 170.21, and 2,000 random states score identically in the app and in the separately written free SPRS calculator. Three low defects the fix did not touch were open on arrival and are fixed here (objective results clear; Level 1 copies pinned equal, which found differing ids for 3.10.4 and 3.14.4; stale flagships entry), plus one new untested guard. Still below the bar on fitness: operational plans of action and enduring exceptions (170.24(b)(1)) cannot be recorded. The sources and the live app could not be loaded today (proxy refused eCFR, NIST, DoD CIO and cmmc.marisstella.app).
